turns.assessment: The simultaneous bidirectional OSC losses on the spans immediately adjacent to S16, together with LOS across many channels and services, indicate a hard physical break rather than a client, transponder, WSS, or amplifier fault. The matching alarms on the S16–S03 and S16–S07 routes suggest that co-routed cables near S16 were struck in one event; the S16–S03 first span is used as the repair anchor. A severe span-loss event is possible but less consistent with the abrupt, complete loss.

proposals.rationale: O87/O89 identify loss of the OSC in both directions over the same physical span adjacent to S16. The simultaneous corresponding losses on S16–S07 are characteristic of an excavation or similar event cutting multiple cables in a shared corridor.
A sufficiently large added loss could also suppress both traffic and OSC, but the abrupt complete multi-cable outage is more characteristic of a cut.
O88/O90 independently localize a bidirectional break to the first physical span on S16–S07; this is likely collateral damage from the same event rather than the sole fault location.
